TheoremBench: Evaluating LLMs on Theorem Proving in Formal Mathematics
variants: Premises/context ablation (easy vs normal / premised vs plain)
controls.detail: Evaluate with full project lemmas/premises vs restricted context or standalone statements.
controls.rules_out: That performance differences reflect only access to auxiliary lemmas/premises rather than core reasoning capability.

controls.name: Weaker baselines
evidence: RLMEval: Evaluating Research-Level Neural Theorem Proving
TheoremBench: Evaluating LLMs on Theorem Proving in Formal Mathematics
controls.detail: Include a general math-pretrained baseline and/or a non-reasoning SFT baseline alongside specialized provers.
controls.rules_out: That gains are attributable to generic pretraining/size rather than specialized reasoning methods.

controls.name: Zero-shot vs few-shot vs retrieved exemplars
evidence: Consistent Autoformalization for Constructing Mathematical Libraries
MathAtlas: A Benchmark for Autoformalization in the Wild
controls.detail: Compare zero-shot, fixed k-shot, and retrieval-augmented exemplars for identical models/prompts.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are due only to having any exemplars rather than exemplar relevance from retrieval.

controls.name: Distilled vs source/base models
evidence: StructFlowBench: A Structured Flow Benchmark for Multi-turn Instruction Following
controls.detail: Evaluate distilled variants and their source/base models in the same pipeline.
controls.rules_out: That differences are explained solely by base-model architecture/size rather than distillation effects.

controls.name: Endpoint and parameter sanity checks
evidence: When Models Can't Follow: Testing Instruction Adherence Across 256 LLMs
controls.detail: Pre-verify endpoints and omit unsupported API parameters; enforce evaluation timeouts.
controls.rules_out: That failures are caused by non-functional endpoints, timeouts, or malformed requests rather than model behavior.

controls.name: Local context ablation
evidence: MathAtlas: A Benchmark for Autoformalization in the Wild
controls.detail: Add/remove immediate local context tokens around the source and compare performance.
controls.rules_out: That gains are solely due to local contextual cues rather than core modeling improvements.

controls.name: Multi-language vs single-language training
evidence: Multi-language Diversity Benefits Autoformalization
controls.detail: Train on joint multi-language data vs each language alone for the same steps.
controls.rules_out: That gains come from extra exposure to one language rather than cross-language transfer.

controls.name: Plain-main baseline for premised theorems
evidence: TheoremBench: Evaluating LLMs on Theorem Proving in Formal Mathematics
controls.detail: Evaluate the same theorems without explicit premise binding and compare pass@k.
controls.rules_out: That premised improvements come from dataset differences rather than explicit premise exposure.

controls.name: Strict vs flexible verification scoring
evidence: When Models Can't Follow: Testing Instruction Adherence Across 256 LLMs
controls.detail: Re-score outputs allowing benign formatting differences to confirm strict-matching results are not artifacts.
controls.rules_out: That low pass rates are due to superficial formatting mismatches rather than substantive failure.

controls.name: Type-check filtering ablation
evidence: Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
controls.detail: Compare sampling+selection with and without type-check filtering; include Filter+Random to isolate filtering from selection heuristics.
controls.rules_out: That gains arise solely from selection heuristics rather than from eliminating ill-typed candidates.

confounds.name: Data contamination / memorization
evidence: MathAtlas: A Benchmark for Autoformalization in the Wild
Multi-language Diversity Benefits Autoformalization
RLMEval: Evaluating Research-Level Neural Theorem Proving
Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
confounds.detail: Models may have seen benchmark data or existing formalisations during training, inflating performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report project first-commit dates vs model cutoffs; analyze grounded-vs-not-grounded items; inspect outputs for copying.

confounds.name: Automatic judge bias or misalignment with humans
evidence: MathAtlas: A Benchmark for Autoformalization in the Wild
Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
StructFlowBench: A Structured Flow Benchmark for Multi-turn Instruction Following
confounds.detail: LLM-as-judge or heuristic metrics may not reflect human semantic faithfulness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Human verification and agreement/correlation analyses (e.g., Cohen's kappa, Pearson/Kendall); select judges aligned with humans.

confounds.name: Sampling budget or selection heuristic, not capability
evidence: RLMEval: Evaluating Research-Level Neural Theorem Proving
Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
TheoremBench: Evaluating LLMs on Theorem Proving in Formal Mathematics
confounds.detail: High pass@k or selection gains may reflect larger k or heuristic choice rather than true model ability.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report low-k (pass@1–2), sweep k, and ablate filtering vs selection to attribute where gains arise.

confounds.name: Type-check rate as a proxy for human correctness
evidence: An Evaluation Benchmark for Autoformalization in Lean4
Multi-language Diversity Benefits Autoformalization
Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
confounds.detail: High type-check rates may not track human-judged correctness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compute correlations between type-check rate and human evaluation; use combined or human-aligned metrics.

confounds.name: Advantage due to available premises/informal proofs
evidence: RLMEval: Evaluating Research-Level Neural Theorem Proving
TheoremBench: Evaluating LLMs on Theorem Proving in Formal Mathematics
confounds.detail: Gains may stem from extra premises or informal hints rather than reasoning ability.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate without premises/informal proofs and compare matched instances.

confounds.name: Compilation/type-check conflates syntax with semantics
evidence: MathAtlas: A Benchmark for Autoformalization in the Wild
Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
confounds.detail: Compiling outputs can be unfaithful to the source despite being syntactically valid.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure semantic faithfulness separately (human or trusted judge) and report Correct = compiles AND faithful.

confounds.name: Differences driven by base LLM capability
evidence: StructFlowBench: A Structured Flow Benchmark for Multi-turn Instruction Following
confounds.detail: Observed performance gaps could arise from base-model choice rather than the proposed pipeline.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Ablations across base LLMs and distillation/source-model comparisons.

confounds.name: Endpoint/API errors masquerading as model failure
evidence: When Models Can't Follow: Testing Instruction Adherence Across 256 LLMs
confounds.detail: Non-functional endpoints, timeouts, or unsupported parameters cause apparent failures.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Pre-verification of endpoints and parameter-aware request construction with enforced timeouts.

confounds.name: Formatting-induced false negatives
evidence: When Models Can't Follow: Testing Instruction Adherence Across 256 LLMs
confounds.detail: Semantically correct responses may be marked wrong due to superficial formatting differences.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Flexible verification pass after strict matching allowing benign formatting/JSON normalization.

confounds.name: Metric bias against long statements
evidence: Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
confounds.detail: Automated equivalence metrics (e.g., BEq+) may have lower recall on longer statements.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure recall vs length and document drops; prefer metrics validated against human judgements.

confounds.name: Noisy informalisation data drives outcomes
evidence: Multi-language Diversity Benefits Autoformalization
confounds.detail: Incorrect or hallucinated informalisations can confound training/evaluation.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Manual audit of informalisation pairs with error categorization and correctness rate reporting.

confounds.name: Observed depth effects due to sampling chance
evidence: MathAtlas: A Benchmark for Autoformalization in the Wild
confounds.detail: Associations between dependency depth and correctness could be sampling artifacts.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Statistical tests on depth distributions (e.g., two-sample KS test) to confirm significance.

confounds.name: Semantic drift from iterative correction/denoising
evidence: Consistent Autoformalization for Constructing Mathematical Libraries
confounds.detail: Refinement steps may fix syntax while drifting from the intended meaning.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Track semantic metrics (e.g., BLEU proxy) alongside Pass across refinement iterations.

confounds.name: Stochastic decoding variability
evidence: When Models Can't Follow: Testing Instruction Adherence Across 256 LLMs
confounds.detail: Randomness in generation can cause inconsistent pass/fail outcomes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Deterministic decoding (temperature=0.0, fixed seed) during evaluation.

experiment_recipes.goal: Endpoints and deterministic decoding sanity check
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On the 20 Diagnostic Test Bank prompts with temperature=0.0 and fixed seed: (1) API success rate >= 0.95 (>= 19/20 successful responses); (2) median response time <= 10 seconds; (3) determinism check: identical outputs across 3 repeated calls on each prompt for >= 0.95 of prompts (>= 19/20). Failing any criterion refutes readiness to proceed.
constraints_not_enforced: Rate-limit behavior outside 20 queries not tested
experiment_recipes.rationale: Pre-verification of endpoints and deterministic decoding prevents conflating ops failures or stochasticity with model behavior, as required by standard VRT evaluation practice.

experiment_recipes.goal: Validated semantic-faithfulness judge aligned with humans
metrics: Semantic faithfulness (Faithful / Correct = Compiles AND Faithful) (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On a stratified random sample of >= 200 model outputs from TheoremBench: (1) Human inter-annotator agreement Cohen's kappa >= 0.60; (2) Correlation of the automatic semantic-faithfulness judge with binarized human acceptability: Pearson r >= 0.70 AND Kendall tau >= 0.60. If any threshold is not met, the automatic judge is not validated and the pipeline fails this apparatus check.
constraints_not_enforced: Potential sampling bias if stratification metadata are limited
depends_on: Endpoints and deterministic decoding sanity check
experiment_recipes.rationale: Standard VRT norms require separating compile success from semantic faithfulness and choosing automatic judges only if they align with human judgments at acceptable reliability.

experiment_recipes.goal: Prover-verified pass@k/compile/correct evaluation for Goedel v2 on TheoremBench
metrics: Semantic faithfulness (Faithful / Correct = Compiles AND Faithful) (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using Lean/Isabelle REPL verification and the validated semantic judge: (1) k-sweep includes exactly k in {1,2,4,32,64,128} with temperature=0.0 for k=1; (2) pass@k (for Correct = Compiles AND Faithful) is non-decreasing across the sweep (no decreases > 0.0 when moving to larger k); (3) >= 95% of instances have a compile/type-check attempt recorded; (4) For >= 90% of compiled outputs, semantic faithfulness is scored by the validated judge. Any violation fails this headline adherence-to-norms check.
constraints_not_enforced: Documenting decoding hyperparameters per checkpoint is not enforced here
depends_on: Validated semantic-faithfulness judge aligned with humans
Endpoints and deterministic decoding sanity check
experiment_recipes.rationale: This enforces core VRT norms: sampling-based evaluation with pass@k scaling, programmatic proof checking, and reporting both syntactic and semantic correctness.

experiment_recipes.goal: Type-check filtering ablation at matched sampling budget
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On an identical instance set with k=32 samples/instance, run three matched-budget pipelines: (A) NoFilter+Random, (B) Filter+Random (select uniformly from type-check-passing candidates), (C) Filter+BestOf (your selection heuristic on type-check-passing pool). Requirements: (1) Candidate budget equality: exactly 32 raw samples per instance in all A/B/C; (2) Filtering effect: mean fraction of eliminated ill-typed candidates in B or C relative to A is >= 0.05. Failure of (1) or (2) refutes that the ablation was run to standard and that filtering had a non-trivial role.
constraints_not_enforced: Specific selection heuristic in C not standardized beyond being a deterministic best-of rule
depends_on: Prover-verified pass@k/compile/correct evaluation for Goedel v2 on TheoremBench
experiment_recipes.rationale: VRT norms attribute gains by ablating type-check filtering versus selection heuristics under matched budgets; ensuring non-trivial filtering guards against selection-only artifacts.

experiment_recipes.goal: Strict vs flexible scorer delta audit
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: At k=32 on the same instance set: (1) Compute strict and flexible pass@32 (Correct) for 100% of evaluated instances; (2) Absolute difference (flexible − strict) in Correct pass@32 <= 0.10 (10 percentage points). Violating (1) fails the protocol adherence; violating (2) indicates formatting-induced false negatives dominate, refuting strict-only adequacy per norms.
constraints_not_enforced: Exact normalization/whitelist rules for flexible scoring not standardized beyond benign formatting allowances
depends_on: Prover-verified pass@k/compile/correct evaluation for Goedel v2 on TheoremBench
experiment_recipes.rationale: Two-stage scoring is a standard control to ensure strict matching is not overly punitive; bounding the delta confirms conclusions are not artifacts of formatting.
